speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent; I understand your newborn is experiencing feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting. Can you tell me when these symptoms first began and if the baby has had any bowel movements yet?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the newborn passed any meconium yet, and if so, how many stools has he had since birth? Also, is there any visible abdominal distension or tenderness upon palpation?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.

speaker: Doctor
text: I notice the baby has not passed meconium yet, which is concerning given the bilious vomiting. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray to check for bowel obstruction or a double-bubble sign.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal X-Ray shows a 'double bubble' sign indicative of duodenal atresia.
